system.name: Tai Chi
system.one_liner: a hardware/software co-designed SmartNIC scheduler that coordinates control-plane tasks and data-plane services via a hybrid virtualization unifying physical and virtual CPUs

content.subject: how Tai Chi registers a vCPU as a native CPU and then intercepts/routes each inter-processor interrupt via source/destination CPU-state checks

elements.name: vCPU1
elements.role: the virtual CPU being created and registered, timeline shown at top of panel (a)

elements.name: OS
elements.role: operating system timeline; hosts the Unified IPI Orchestrator that intercepts boot IPIs

elements.name: CPU0
elements.role: physical CPU timeline that sends the initialization/startup IPIs driving vCPU1's activation

elements.name: Unified IPI Orchestrator
elements.role: intercepts every IPI transmission and routes it according to source/destination CPU state

elements.name: Creating vCPU1
elements.role: event marking when the OS creates vCPU1 with metadata such as CPU ID and LAPIC ID

elements.name: Initializing vCPU1
elements.role: first CPU0 phase, sending the IPIs that begin activating vCPU1

elements.name: Startuping vCPU1
elements.role: second CPU0 phase continuing vCPU1's boot sequence

elements.name: Responding
elements.role: final CPU0 phase after which vCPU1 is online and treated as a native CPU

elements.name: vCPU or pCPU
elements.role: the IPI's originating processor, entering the routing logic in panel (b)

elements.name: Source CPU state?
elements.role: decision testing whether the source is a physical (P) or virtual (V) CPU

elements.name: vCPU scheduler
elements.role: invoked on a VM-exit when the source is a vCPU; reissues the IPI so it propagates across the virtualization boundary

elements.name: Destination CPU state?
elements.role: decision testing whether the destination is a physical (P) or virtual (V) CPU

elements.name: Injecting IPIs
elements.role: outcome when the destination is a vCPU; the orchestrator injects the IPI directly, waking a sleeping vCPU first if needed

elements.name: writing MSR to send IPIs
elements.role: outcome when the destination is a pCPU; delivered via a low-level Model-Specific Register write

relations.what: the OS creates vCPU1 with metadata (CPU ID, LAPIC ID) and registers it, initially offline
CPU0 sends boot-related IPIs (Initializing, Startuping, Responding) that the orchestrator intercepts
the orchestrator routes the intercepted IPIs to vCPU1, activating it until it is treated as a native CPU
a vCPU source triggers a VM-exit, handing control to the vCPU scheduler, which reissues the IPI
the reissued IPI (now as pCPU) proceeds to the destination-side state check
a vCPU destination gets the IPI injected directly, woken first if sleeping
a pCPU destination gets the IPI delivered via a low-level MSR write

transitions.guard: source CPU state = V, triggering a VM-exit
IPI reissued so it propagates across the virtualization boundary
destination CPU state = V (runnable/running, or woken if sleeping)

decisions.question: Source CPU state?
branches: pCPU: no special action, proceed directly
vCPU: VM-exit to the vCPU scheduler, which reissues the IPI

decisions.question: Destination CPU state?
branches: pCPU: deliver via low-level MSR write
vCPU: inject the IPI directly, waking it first if sleeping

content.key_idea: The Unified IPI Orchestrator delivers the boot IPIs that turn a new vCPU into a native CPU, and for every later IPI checks source/destination CPU state to route it via the vCPU scheduler or deliver it directly.
content.reading_order: left to right along each of the three timelines in (a), top to bottom through the source-state then destination-state decision diamonds in (b)

palette.used_for: gray fill of the three active named boxes (Unified IPI Orchestrator, vCPU scheduler, vCPU or pCPU)

evidence: the vCPU scheduler creates vCPUs with metadata (e.g., CPU ID, LAPIC ID) and registers them with the OS
IPIs involve source CPU and destination CPU
no special action is taken if the source CPU is a pCPU

summary: Figure 8 shows two related mechanisms inside Tai Chi's unified IPI orchestrator. In (a) Registering vCPU as native CPU, a 3-lane timeline traces how the vCPU scheduler creates vCPU1 (initially offline); CPU0 then sends a sequence of boot-related IPIs, Initializing vCPU1, Startuping vCPU1, Responding, which the orchestrator intercepts and routes to vCPU1 until the OS treats it as a native CPU. In (b) Intercepting and routing IPI, every IPI from a vCPU or pCPU first hits a Source CPU state decision: a pCPU source proceeds directly, while a vCPU source triggers a VM-exit so the vCPU scheduler reissues it. A second Destination CPU state decision then either injects the IPI into a vCPU, waking it first if sleeping, or writes an MSR to deliver it to a pCPU.
